issues.description: IAM-policy fetch failure silently produces PASS instead of UNKNOWN/ERROR.
issues.detail: When getIamPolicy raises (e.g. permission denied on fixture image 3), the except branch logs and leaves publicly_shared=False, so the check reports PASS for an image whose sharing state was never read. An auth error becoming a clean bill of health is the worst failure mode for a security check. Introduce a tri-state or separate retrieved flag and emit a distinct finding.

issues.description: Naming inconsistency between PR description, CheckID/directory, and the publicly_shared data field.
issues.detail: PR text references compute_image_publicly_shared while the directory, CheckID, class, and CHANGELOG use compute_image_not_publicly_shared, and the model field is the positive publicly_shared. Pick one direction and align metadata, path, and field so PASS semantics are unambiguous to the next reader.

issues.description: Image listing does not filter custom vs public/deprecated images as the spec claims.
issues.detail: The PR states the check evaluates only custom images, but images().list(project=project_id) is called with no filter (e.g. deprecated.state, family, source). Either enforce the precondition with an explicit filter or document why none is required, otherwise the check will produce noisy or incorrect findings.

issues.description: Bare except Exception swallows programmer errors and is inconsistent with threaded collection style.
issues.detail: Both try blocks catch Exception without narrowing, so KeyError/TypeError from malformed responses are logged as if they were API permission errors. Additionally, _get_images iterates project_ids serially while every other resource in compute_service.py uses __threading_call__. Narrow the exception handling and match the file's existing threading idiom.

issues.description: Public-member detection is complected with I/O; bindings evidence is discarded.
issues.detail: _get_images interleaves project iteration, pagination, IAM fetch, error handling, and the allAuthenticatedUsers scan in one nested block, then collapses the bindings into a single boolean on the Image value. Extract the bindings->bool rule as a pure function and preserve the offending role/binding on the model so it is testable and auditable.

issues.description: Tests never exercise the IAM-failure path at the check layer; they confirm mocks rather than logic.
issues.detail: Fixture image 3 triggers an exception in getIamPolicy and the service test merely asserts publicly_shared is False, masking the failure. Check-level tests construct Image objects with publicly_shared pre-set, so the bindings transformation is never exercised end-to-end. Add a check-layer test for the unknown-policy case and unit-test the pure rule directly.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees the check is small and follows surrounding idioms on the happy path, but has one consequential security defect: an IAM-policy fetch failure silently yields PASS, conflating UNKNOWN with safe. Naming is inconsistent across PR text, directory/CheckID, and the positive publicly_shared field, signaling weak spec discipline. The image listing does not establish the "custom images only" precondition it claims. Lower-priority concerns: bare exception handling, missing threading consistency, complected I/O and pure rule logic, and tests that exercise mocks rather than the bindings transformation or the IAM-failure path at the check layer. Verdict: NEEDS-WORK before merge.
